First, the witness, as Your Honour has pointed out, said it was well known, which might lead one to believe that it is not the result of an isolated incident. Second of all, and perhaps more importantly, the point that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has raised goes to rehabilitating that witness perhaps on redirect examination and not to the issue of any bias or credibility of the issue -- credibility of the witness which is the specific issue that I'm addressing you on at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll allow you to -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be even briefer -- I think we should be even briefer, because we've spent too much time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, we'll allow you a limited number of questions on the issue. And if one would expect that the Chamber would hold the view that soldiers in opposite armies would feel great friendship towards the soldiers of the other party, that expectation might not be a very realistic one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us that your experience taught you -- taught your community of the VRS that Muslims could not be trusted with respect to their agreements. Did your experience teach you any other lessons with respect to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be clearer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to ask the question to you. You say that experience taught you that Muslims rarely respected agreements reached. Are there other things you -- your experience learned you about Muslims such -- it could be whatever, being very good drivers or being in general friendly people when you meet them or -- whatever. Do you have any other view on Muslims based upon your experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before the war, I lived in an environment that was multi-ethnic and I had good relations with Muslims who went to the same school as I did. We went to university together. We were on good terms. It is this war that hit us, that changed the whole situation, and they showed a totally different image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from what -- respecting the agreements, what else was part of this changed image? What other respects changed your perception of Muslims caused by the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a question of understanding by the witness. I'm not quite sure that you used the word "respect."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I said is in what other respect. So you mentioned one that Muslims would rarely respect agreements reached. That's one aspect you mentioned. Were there any other aspects -- I might have said aspects. I'm not quite sure. Was your view on Muslims changed in other aspects as well? Because you told us that your view on Muslims was completely changed by the war. If you don't understand my question, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to ask it then in a different way. You told us that experience learned you that Muslims would rarely respect agreements. You also told us that your view on Muslims - and you lived with them before the war in normal circumstances - was completely changed by the war. You mentioned this one aspect, that they would not respect agreements. In what other aspects -- would you, for example, say that -- whatever other aspect, other than the one already mentioned, changed your view on Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us say, for instance, their attitude towards us as a nation, towards our religion, culture, traditions, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be the most important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very rapidly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, to a question of the Prosecution, you were asked if you were in charge of the whole area covered by the Corps of the Sarajevo-Romanija. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. You were asked about your area of responsibility and what it was. What did you answer to that question? Not for you personally. What I mean is for the military police.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking about the area of the city of Sarajevo, where we went, that is, the Grbavica, Lukavica, Ilidza, that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the duties that you had, did you have any knowledge of the importance of the length of the front line in its entirety with respect to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was about 230 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You gave us answers about the automatic mode and the single-shot mode for certain weapons, standard weapons. Could you confirm that the instructions were given in general, if that is the case, not to open fire except as returning fire, in response.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you spoke to us about the attitude of the Muslims towards your culture and your religion. On this subject, do you know if in Sarajevo at present the street names have been changed?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have only the street names -- the Serb street names changed?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you tell us about the attitude of Muslims towards your culture and your religion, with respect to your religion what do you mean exactly? Could you tell us in a nutshell, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you make it clearer a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I will. You spoke to us about their attitude towards your religion. For instance, any unpleasant remarks, racist attitudes? Are you talking about any destructive attitudes? And by this I mean in the most general terms, in terms of religion, have you ever had any experience of that? I'm going to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis. If -- Yes, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was the attitude in general of the Muslims in terms of the religious aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, this calls for complete speculation, and we also question it on the grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will let you decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us, how do you experience the changed attitude of Muslims in respect of your religion - I don't know what your personal religion is, but I would say the religion which is the prevailing one under the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you experience that? I mean, what do you observe? How does that feel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I noticed that there was a lot of ignorance, something -- that's usually something that didn't exist, something that was of lesser value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you experienced the change in the appreciation of your religion by the Muslims; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one question for you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am a little bit confused about one issue, so I would like you to clarify that for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The question is the following: Your military police battalion was the only one within the brigade or within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got one question for you. You -- perhaps more than one. You told us that your barracks where the police company was established in Lukavica was not in the same building as the headquarters of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your building, was that a multi-storey building or just a one-storey building?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two floors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two floors. The other building of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps headquarters where you stood guard, was that also a two-storey building?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had the ground floor and one upstairs, one upper floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the same as your own building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was lower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was lower. So when you say your building had two floors, that means one ground floor and two upper floors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You -- did you ever go to the first upper floor, that is, the top floor, of the building of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went rarely because refugees were there. They were housed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in the upper floor of the headquarters of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps there were refugees there, or did I understand you --

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of the command but of the building where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me ask you quite clearly. You have answered a question of what you could see from the top floor in Lukavica barracks, especially whether you could see buildings or whether you could look behind buildings at a distance. What top floor did you understand was the question about?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the floor where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that means your building, one ground floor, two upper floors, and there the top floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. This concludes your testimony in this court -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question which stems from your questions, Mr. President. Just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please keep in mind that top floor was already raised in chief and it was not something I raised for the first time. Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But the question is the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bearing in mind, witness, of the location of the buildings, the other building where General Galic was, in relation to Dobrinja, your testimony is that you could see even less from the building where General Galic was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes your testimony in this court. Mr. Vukovic, I'd like to -- Yes. I -- whenever I try to say that this concludes the testimony of someone in this court, Mr. Vukovic, someone thinks that it might not have been the conclusion yet. Mr. Mundis, is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could, based on the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and it goes to the foundation of the witness's last response and whether that could be perhaps clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's really the last question now. One more question for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, when asked if you could see even less from the building where General Galic was, you answered yes. My question is: Were you ever on the top floor of the building that housed the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and if you ever looked out the window of that building?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the question. The witness answered that he had gone into an office which was located somewhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let's first -- could you take your earphones off. As far as my recollection goes, the witness testified that he went to the first floor but the second part of the question is not yet answered. So perhaps you can put to the witness what his testimony was and ask, then that, additional question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're attempting to locate the previous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was on one of my -- it was in response of one of my questions, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, when you were on the top floor of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps building, did you ever look out the window?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that Mr. -- that was your question, Mr. Mundis. Then this really concludes your testimony in the court, Mr. Vukovic. I know that it's a long way, and I can imagine that it's -- it's not always easy to testify about things that have not only left perhaps nice memories. I thank you very much for coming. I thank you very much for answering the questions of both parties and of the Judges, and I hope that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may avail myself of this opportunity while the witness is leaving. The Defence would like to inform the Chamber that we will have a problem with the following witness since he has to leave tomorrow morning. We did not expect that the cross-examination of Mr. Vukovic would take such a long time. And yesterday from the Victims and Witnesses Unit we were informed that he had to leave tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I just make an observation about that. As I said yesterday, there is a difficulty with the timetable which the Defence has provided us with their witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It doesn't allow for cross-examination. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you have explained to us what in the view of the Prosecution is one of the reasons why. What we could do is now just see how far question come. That's what we did before. What I know is that we have approximately available another 40 minutes until the break and then almost an hour. That would not be the time you estimated, but the Chamber was very pleased to observe that you used less time for the last witness as indicated before. Let's just try to see where we come and let's try to do this as efficiently as possible and see what we can do, rather than at this moment discuss the reasons and the necessity of the witness to travel back. Could you -- perhaps we should first deal with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to see what we can do, we'd rather deal with the documents and tapes tomorrow, especially because there might be some technical problems with it as well. I'd first like to turn into private session to -- since no decision has yet been taken on protective measures sought by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. It doesn't matter, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration. And the text will be handed to you now by the usher. Would you please stand up while making that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic can we start in open session or would you like to return to private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it would be better that we go into private session because I will show the witness a document immediately and ask for some data about the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll turn into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, you told us where you were detained. Before I move on to other questions, can you tell me whether you know as to whether that building in 1992, 1993, and 1994 continued to be used to imprison Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes. It was used as some sort of a local prison, and various Serbs were brought in for information interviews and were mistreated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP8, you told us that in May 1992 you were a minor. I will ask you some questions covering the period September 1992 until August 1994. Can you tell us where you were in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: In September 1992 I was in Nedzarici as a member of the army. I had just returned from treatment and I joined the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it is that you joined the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At the end of May. In 1992 I returned, and that is when I joined the army, because I had undergone medical treatment for the injuries sustained before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, when you say that you became a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, can you tell us which military unit you belonged to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At the time it was some sort of Territorial Defence. There were patrols that people organised by themselves in Nedzarici as some sort of defence. We wouldn't let anyone enter Nedzarici. Checks were made of people passing through Nedzarici. We weren't really armed. I was a sort of courier in those days in Nedzarici because I was under 18 years of age and I hadn't done my military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in September 1992 this military unit that you belonged to, was it the Territorial Defence or was it a military unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: It was a military unit within the 1st Battalion of Nedzarici. We called it an armoured company. We had two or three armoured vehicles which were faulty and they stayed behind in the Nedzarici barracks after the Army of Yugoslavia left and then they were repaired to some extent and they were given to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say that you were a member of an armoured company of the 1st Battalion, can you tell us how many men there were in your company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: There was about 15 men in our company. But when pulling out the dead or the wounded or delivering food to the separation lines, we used the APCs for pulling out the dead and the wounded and for distributing food to the people who were already on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, I'll stop you for a moment. You say that there were 15 of you in the company. Who was the company commander? Did you have a commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The company commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you can't tell us his name or you don't want to tell us his name --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I can give you the nickname. Miso was the nickname of the commander of the armoured company at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8 -- you had I don't company commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who was your superior, superior to the company and the company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which battalion did your company belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your company commander, who did he get orders from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: From the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the command of the battalion was quartered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The command of the 1st Battalion was quartered at the barracks in Nedzarici in one of the buildings in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, for the duration of the conflict - and we're focussing on 1992 to September 1994 - did the command post of the 1st Battalion always -- was it always in that same position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No, not always.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when, if you know, it was moved, that is, the command post of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The command post until the beginning of 1993 was in Nedzarici and constantly in the barracks, until up to the beginning of 1993 when there was a kind of reorginisation when the Kasindol Street, Nedzarici and the airport united and that is when it became the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, can you tell us in which street -- could you repeat where the command post of the 1st Battalion was later on, that is, when it was moved from Nedzarici it was at the beginning of the Kasindol Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I don't know the exact name that it has now, but I know where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP8, you told us that you were a member of an armoured company. Can you tell us whether you had a command post.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- yes, I'm sorry. Mr. DP8, can you tell us where the command post of your company was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The command post of my company was for a time in the barracks. That must have been in June. And then towards the end of 1992 we moved to the Croatian monastery or the theology faculty, as it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You were in the theology faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, can you tell us whether you spent any time in that building and how much time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In the period of about one year, until the company command moved to Ilidza under the protection of UNPROFOR, when the headquarters was moved there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, can you be more precise. When you said that you were at the building of the theology faculty, can you tell us until when? You said the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes. I went there all the time, because the ambulance -- the clinic was there. I would bring the wounded to the nunnery because there was a medical service. People who were working in the medical service were extending first aid there and then they were transferred on to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll come back to the building of the theology faculty, but you were not precise as to when you moved to the Energoinvest building. Can you can you tell us when you moved to the Energoinvest building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: That happened towards the end of 1993. At least that is what I think. I don't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, let us clarify your answers. You said that you were at the theology faculty until the end of 1992, after which you moved to the Energoinvest building. And now you told us that you moved to the Energoinvest building at the end of 1993. Can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I said that at first we were in the barracks. That is where the headquarters were. So shall we say in September 1992 we moved to the nunnery. We stayed there until the end of 1993, when UNPROFOR came, or rather, Ukrainian soldiers who held guard duty in the Energoinvest factory. We had a hall there where all our armoured vehicles were parked, all the armoured vehicles of the brigade were then under the supervision of the Ukrainian unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP8, when you say that in 1993 you had your command post at the theology faculty, you said that also the medical service was accommodated there. Were there any other military units accommodated there as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The medical corps, us, our company, and some advance positions of mortars, and the people manning the mortars were also accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, in the period from 1992 through to 1994, who or, rather, were you as members of the company issued orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the duration of the war we were given orders by the company commander normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "throughout the duration of the war by the company commander," can you tell us how frequent such orders were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At any point in time when there was shooting -- and it was very frequent in Nedzarici. The Muslims were opening fire on Nedzarici non-stop, and somebody would regularly be wounded and you would be given orders where to pick up the wounded or a killed combatant or whatever. And communication used was a telephone. The company commander probably got his orders from the battalion commander, and he would send us to the spot where we would have to carry out our assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You said that in Nedzarici combat was frequent. I think that is what you said, that fire was opened very frequently. Can you tell us from which positions the fire on Nedzarici came.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The Nedzarici settlement was shot at from all the various positions. Nedzarici was in a valley, so fire was opened from the new old people's home close to the Oslobodjne building. Then the Oslobodjne building itself was a high building, so it was very useful. Then there were two student hostel buildings. Then in Vojnicko Polje, Dobrinja V and Mojmilo Hill. These were suitable for shooting, and they had a recoilless gun located there, which they used to fire at Nedzarici throughout the duration of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you told us that these buildings were used, the buildings that you listed, can you tell us with regard to the buildings in Vojnicko Polje and Mojmilo. First, how high those buildings are, how many storeys.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Between six and eight storeys. The buildings in Vojnicko Polje, in Dobrinja V -- again, buildings have between six and eight floors. But Oslobodjne building was higher. But it was on a lower -- built at a lower level, so the top was on the same level more or less as the buildings in Vojnicko Polje and Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With regard to the building in Vojnicko Polje and Dobrinja V that you told us about, do you personally know from which floors fire was opened and using which weapons by the Army of BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I know personally because my house that I went to every day and where my mother lived was very close to Dobrinja V. And to get to my house, I had to use a lot of shortcuts and various protective screens against rifle shots were put up. So I was never safe. In approaching Dobrinja V or Vojnicko Polje or if I had to go anywhere else to familiarise myself with a location for the purpose of delivering food the next day or for saving the wounded, I was never safe along that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In answer to a question from the defence, you told us what kind of orders you were given when it came to orders to pull out the wounded or to engage in combat. In addition to those orders, did you receive any other orders from your superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At any point in time there would be meetings where the company leaders would meet with the battalion commander and they would discuss things and then the company leader would give us warnings and tell us that we shouldn't move around unnecessarily, that we shouldn't open fire unnecessarily but only in self-defence or in response to an attack by the Muslim army, that we should respond with fire, things like that, that we wouldn't -- that we shouldn't use our vehicles unnecessarily, that we should save on petrol and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8 --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I say something in closed session very quickly before we break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we'll first ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'll have a break for 20 minutes, Mr. DP8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn in to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait until the accused has arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, maybe I could use that time by raising a procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In open session, I take it. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We're taking steps to have a French-speaking person available to us so that we can at least have some idea of the correspondence given to us in French and hopefully that will speed hat matters up. Secondly, in the last few weeks Mr. Piletta-Zanin has been speaking to us in French at meetings, which seems to negate the advantage of having an English-speaking Defence counsel. Might I respectfully suggest that if meetings were conducted at the senior trial attorney level, that might smooth matters to some extent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may respond --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With just as much time as Mr. Ierace took.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even less time than that. Mr. Ierace, what were the words that I used in French, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that in the meetings that Mr. Ierace told us that you either spoke or insisted on speaking French.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Mr. President. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's -- the language used in the out-of-court meetings of the parties might not be an issue that needs a lot of attention, if we're trying to hurry in such a way that we can see whether we can finish with this witness today. So it's not the appropriate time now to continue the discussion we heard of Mr. Ierace -- we heard your response -- until now. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, before the break you spoke to us about the buildings that you told us were used by the BH army and from which buildings firing was directed in Nedzarici. Could you tell us, considering that you lived there, what buildings were dominating in the Nedzarici settlement, bearing in mind that we know that this is a settlement with family houses. Could you tell us what are the houses that are higher than the family houses in the Nedzarici settlement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The theological faculty in Nedzarici, the monastery building, as we called it. This is one of taller buildings and the rest were houses with one or two stories, mostly with one storey in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The period September 1992 to August 1994 you told us that you were in the building of the theological faculty. Did you visit the building of the Institute for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The entire line that was in the Nedzarici I visited it. I went there. So I would go to the location to see how I would get to a wounded, or to bring food, what would be the safest route to take. So I was on all the demarcation lines of the VRS and of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, could you tell us, in the building of the Institute for the Blind, were there soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: In the building of the Institute for the Blind, there were Serbian soldiers. There was a platoon of the army, and they held this position on the front line. This is where their positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP, when we're speaking about the Institute for the Blind, in relation to the demarcation lines -- in relation to the Institute for the Blind, how far were the demarcation lines of both armies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The entire line in Nedzarici, there was a very little distance between the two demarcation lines of the BH army and the Republika Srpska army. In some places only 4 or 5 metres, so there would just be a street between them. So the road that would be going in them, in one building there would be Muslims and then in the other opposite there would be Serbs. So in some places there would be a distance of only 5 to 6 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence would like to show the witness several photographs, Prosecution exhibits. The Defence has stated in the exhibit list what these are, and we also have these photographs. With your leave in order to speed up, maybe they could be put on the ELMO. The photograph is 3277 that we would like shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar just checks whether there are any documents admitted under seal, Ms. Pilipovic. I take that the Prosecution can check whether these are the right photographs by looking at them on the ELMO, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. You may just put them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, do you recognise this photograph? Do you recognise what you see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, on this photograph can you see the Institute for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: On this photograph, you cannot see it clearly, the Institute for the Blind. It should be alongside this road, so it would be at the end of this street, which is -- which goes below this house in Vojnicko Polje. It's partly hiding it, this and also these -- these trees. This was in the Aleja Branka Bujica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in relation to the student hostel buildings, in your opinion, could you tell us what was the view from the Institute of the Blind towards this street? Could you tell us what was the name of this large street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This one or that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This large one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This large street, I don't know what it's called. I know that it -- there was -- between the Vojnicko Polje and Alipasino that's where it was located. I don't know its name. And this street that goes down there, this was Aleja Branka Bujica Street. That's what it was called. It demarcated the Nedzarici locality and the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When we look at this street, the Aleja Branka Bujica Street that you indicated for us, could you tell us in the period from September of 1992 until August of 1994 what part -- or was this street used in its entirety by the BH army or by the VRS? Where were the demarcation lines in relation to this street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The demarcation lines were by the Institute for the Blind and the old school, that is, Centre for the Blind, this is where the bind people worked, and this is where it ended. It ended on an intersection in front of the Centre for the Blind. But this street entirely until the student hostel -- this student hostel -- and there's another building of the student hostel, so this is not the only one. So this entire part was held by the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the relevant period of time that we are talking about while you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think it's clear from the transcript what area the witness was referring to when he said "so this entire part was held by the Muslim army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's -- he referred to the street that is --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Aleja Branka Bujica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the parties would agree what Aleja Branka Bujica Street would be, then it would be clear. The name of the street has been mentioned many, many times. That's the street that goes up to the Institute for the Blind. Would that be sufficient, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Plead please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, for the relevant period of time, considering that you told us that you went to the Institute for the Blind, could you tell us whether from these positions did you have a view towards this intersection, this intersection that we see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Well, from any point that I looked at from the Institute for the Blind, because there were trenches by the Institute for the Blind -- you couldn't see the intersection because all the streets on the Serb and on the Muslim side that were near the demarcation line were protected. I've already said this was an area with a kind of screen or containers with old curtains, blankets, and so on, whatever was found to put up a protection, protective screens. And in this street in three places there were screens put up. One of them went all the way up to the intersection, and some trenches that they had, according to the storeys, that was hidden which linked up the student hostel and Vojnicko Polje. There was also a screen there. And on the demarcation line itself by the market centre, shopping centre and some businesses privately owned, in front of the building of the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP8.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now we would like to show the witness another photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. And if it will be put on the ELMO in such a way -- let me just have a look. That's -- yes, that's not a -- an exhibit that has been admitted under seal, so it can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to -- just have to be very careful. There's a name on the photograph. Is that a protected name? I don't think so, but -- no. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, the building that you see in front on the photograph which seems to have a fence on it, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes, I do. One building -- in fact, there are three buildings which seemed to have fences on them. Which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The first one, the one which has -- which is the longest in front.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: You mean this one? Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, during the conflict from 1992 through 1994, was this building damaged? And if it was, where and what was the state of this house at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This house during the period of time, I think that it was slightly smaller. You couldn't see it from this first building, which means this -- on this house it says it's a bakers. Before, it used to be a coffee bar, a restaurant, and you couldn't see at all this building from this other building. I'm absolutely certain -- I don't think. I'm absolutely certain that after the war it was -- there was extra built on it. There was an addition built, an extension build.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you told us the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't follow. Which is the first building from which one could not see the bakery building, if that's what the witness is saying? The point is that the transcript does not make that clear, let alone my lack of understanding of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you just try to clarify the issue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, are you telling us that the house -- that the building that we see in the front of the photograph, in the corner of the photograph to the right, where there are some kind of fences put on it, is this the building which hides the bakers --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The building that we see in the front in the right-hand corner, which has lines over it, that you described in the lower right corner with the red roof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this building was hiding the building behind which says "bakers" on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No. I said that the building with the bakers on was hiding before the building which can now be seen. It was behind it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness has just said that the building which is smaller which is in the centre of photograph, which says "baker," the witness has just told us that this building with baker on used to hide the building that is now in the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now that you told us all this, can you tell us in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still not very much clear. Witness, could you please first point at the building that was hiding another building. Which was the building that did hide another building? Is that the whole of that building or just the wide part with the small red roof? Could you encircle the building --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This building of the bakers goes alongside this long building at the front that I said that could not be seen at all from Nedzarici. You couldn't see it. You could only see it from the sports hall looking towards the Oslobodjne building. Now, from this side to the right, that's where it was, and it was not possible to see this building which you can see here in the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. The whole of the building with the red roof that -- where we find the black markings on, that whole building was not visible, you said, from the -- if you were looking at it from the -- from Nedzarici? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that clear, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, you told us -- you mentioned student hostels. You said that it was used by the BH army. Could you tell us in what state were the buildings in? Were they damaged, the buildings of the student hostel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Certainly they were damaged, just like all the other buildings in the war. This was where the demarcation line was on both sides of the street, so these buildings were damaged. In some places there were no windows. Some neighbourhoods -- some houses were burnt. You could see all the blackened buildings and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to show the witness another photograph. This is P327900.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. It can be put on the ELMO. It's not protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, do you recognise buildings in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, this building that can be seen in the foreview, if we can call it the white building, which has only one level, just the ground floor. Could you explain to us this building that I am describing now. Could you tell us what was that and did it exist during the conflict at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes, it did exist before the conflict and after the conflict. That was the shopping centre, the market. There were coffee-shops and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, this photograph, the way that it is, the way it appears, could you tell us from which positions could have this photograph been taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I think it was from the lateral side of the building of the Institute for the Blind, which looked on to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, could you tell us, this building, was this facility that was used during the conflict, the one that you described just now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The shopping centre building?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, the white building that you say that's the building of the shopping centre, could you tell us was this facility used and who used it during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Throughout the war it was used and it was used by the BH army, and the entire shopping centre linked to the trenches, to the buildings of the Vojnicko Polje, also hidden by some screens, trenches were used. It was used like a resistance line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are you telling us that soldiers were in this building? Did you see soldiers in that building? Were they there? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: In this building there were soldiers, but they couldn't be seen very frequently because they were well protected. It would be insane to appear, to be seen. Nobody was appearing from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, on this photograph the street that we see, could you tell us which street is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This street to the right which goes in front of the shopping centre is this is this what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This is the Lukavicka Cesta road which goes all the way to Dobrinja V and there was a demarcation of sorts, that I've already explained, that was the demarcation between the Muslim army and the Serbian army. So this was the only street, in this part, which -- which divided the Serb positions from the Muslim positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP8, we're going to show you another photograph now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the transcript, Ms. Pilipovic, Exhibit P327900 has got two numbers. The photograph you just showed was ERN number 01061210/08. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, on this photograph do you recognise the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, this photograph was taken from which positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I think this is Djure Jaksica Street and this photograph was taken behind the building of the earlier mentioned shopping centre from the street itself, behind the building of the shopping centre. That's where it was taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, could you tell us, these build that is we see were these buildings that were used or do you know who used these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This building here on the right that you can see, that was the front line. So in fact, it can be seen on the previous photograph. That is the first building next to Nedzarici and then the front line, it was all for the Muslim soldiers. But all these buildings were linked, all these other buildings through a system of trenches, as I've already explained, and they were hidden by some screens and it was all used by the army. Some companies, as we had information, they used it for a rest, so they had a full military settlement, except that some Serbs lived in the apartments, that they didn't allow to leave, and their families were put in other apartments that used to be Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Your Honour, Mr. DP has pointed to the build that we see both in the middle and that we see on the side of the photograph as the buildings that, according to him, had been used by the soldiers of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are always two sides on the photograph, Ms. Pilipovic. You're referring to the red brick buildings with the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... white one. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both sides, yes. Your Honour, we're talking about the right-hand side of the photograph. This building was pointed by Mr. DP8 as being the building that was on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, do you have any information the building that can be seen on the right-hand side, that is, the red building, do you have any knowledge who used this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Muslim soldiers used it, these buildings here. And this building that can be seen right next to this white building is one building. That means that this is -- they are together, so they were also used by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the building with the red brick structure and not to the building at the right-hand side. Your question was about the right-hand side of the photograph, but the witness was pointing at the left-hand side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this may go to the same point, but on page 89, at line 6, Mrs. Pilipovic said, "This building was pointed by Mr. DP8 as being the building 'that was on the front line'." I don't recollect the witness saying that that building was on the front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness testified that the building where we see a white surface on the right-hand side of the photograph, that that was the building on the front line. Is that correct? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll show it again. This is the building that was right next to the front line, next to the demarcation line of the Serb army and the Muslim army. And this is the building where Muslim units were in throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's entirely clear. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague will ask a few more questions so that we can be more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course I'm looking at the clock at this very moment. I don't know how much time the Prosecution would need to cross-examine the witness. We know that we lost a quarter of an hour on protective measures, unnecessarily. And of course you have apologised to that. But let's just see -- and may I urge the parties to be as efficient as possible. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. What is the next number in order for our exhibits, please? 73?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly what we have. I should like to submit this exhibit D1173 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, D1773.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do you recognise this map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, would you use the pointer and point to the circle that is in the middle of the map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you tell us briefly what was within that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Within that circle there were houses, that is, Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm interrupting you, witness. I'm talking about the inside of the red circle, not the zone. Within the red circle, what was within that red circle during the war, please? Maybe it's black for you, but originally it was red. What is within the circle that you pointed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: There were houses within that circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I can't see what you're showing, as we have no picture on the video. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It's the circle in the middle. Yes. Thank you very much. Witness, could you please tell us now, to the right of that circle -- point the pointer to the right of that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Here. That's right. In the area you're pointing to, in all -- throughout that area, between the red dot and the point that you are pointing to, that is, before the first building, what was there during the war -- during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: During the war there were private houses here which were mostly owned by Muslims, and somewhere here was a Muslim mosque, a religious Muslim building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Actually, between the point that you have just indicated and point number 22, was it possible for a direct shot with a light weapon to intervene; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very briefly, why is it not possible for a direct shot with a small arms fire could hit this distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Because those buildings were in front of the Serb lines that were an obstacle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The same question regarding the second circle on the left. Point the pointer at the circle to the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you slow down because this is too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Mr. President, I don't think again that it's at all clear from the transcript the area indicated by the witness where there was a mosque and other buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness pointed to an area slightly to the right of the area inhabited by Muslims that he pointed to a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the same question regarding the point to the extreme left --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't think that is sufficient. If you take a different view, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But on my reading of the transcript it is not at all clear to anyone who reads the transcript which area the witness was talking to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness was pointing at an area a little bit below and right from the open circle in the middle of the map going into the direction of number 22 up until where considerable construction seems to appear. So that's the open area with more or less a cross in the middle of it, which seems to appear roads. Please proceed. But marking might be more efficient, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. But I do appreciate that you're trying to do your utmost best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As we are talking about a mosque, was it ever targeted, hit, or destroyed by your forces; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: It was not destroyed or hit. I said earlier on at the meetings held by company commanders with the battalion commander, we were constantly reminded not to target religious facilities, civilian vehicles, if we were to see any, or civilians at all, even people digging a trench. They were treated as an enemy because they were on the front line. We were told to shoot as little as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The circle to the extreme left, please, will you point at it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. The same question as a moment ago: From this point, is it possible directly to hit point 22? If not, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Because from this point one could only see the tops of these first buildings in Dobrinja V.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Perfect. Thank you very much for your answer. We'll go on now to Exhibit 1774, which I'd like to be shown to the witness. Number 13. I think we can leave the map on the side, the previous map for a moment, because in a moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, between the place indicated by the circle in the middle of the map and the point marked "21," is there a direct view between these two points?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, I object, Mr. President. For a start --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The issue is whether there was a direct view on that particular date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, perhaps it would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see whether the witness can answer the question or whether there's any reservation to be made. So the question was, Mr. DP8, whether from the circle in the middle of the photograph up until the dot where we find number 21, whether there was a direct view. And please indicate if this would have been different in time. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate the time pressure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Within the circle, we have -- and I don't think it's in dispute -- the school for the blind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question as phrased means nothing. Does he mean the ground in front of the school for the blind? The first floor? The second floor? Which particular building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin we all know that it might be of importance whether we talk about first floor, ground floor, et cetera, so could you please try to elicit from the witness such information that would assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you take the rule their the usher is going to hand to you and point the ruler, if you can, to point 21 and draw it to the middle of the circle. Between the middle of the circle and point 21. Further up, point 21. Move the ruler further up, please. Witness, a dot marked "21." 21. Not 13 but 21. Now draw a line, please, with a black pain, a fine black pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, the trajectory that you have just drawn passes through a building. This building, was it a student hostel? Did it totally obstruct the view viewing it from the Institute of the Blind regardless of the floor of that building; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is an eloquent leading question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- to invite the witness to draw a line which takes it through a building, according to this map, and then invite the witness to indicate whether it was possible to see the spot. Whatever the witness says now has no weight in view of the way in which my learned colleague has approached that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond, Mr. President? Yes. Yes, I'm at fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you say that you reformulate the question or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no -- I haven't quite understood -- no, I didn't say -- I'm sorry. It's a way of protesting vehemently.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter corrects itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was never at fault. I am protesting against this assertion of the Prosecution for the simple and good reason, Mr. President, that we asked about the view, then we were told that we had to ask from which floor. And I'm doing it now. Whether I asked for a line to be drawn before or after, the reality remains the same. The view goes through the building. The line goes through the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The line goes through the building. That's for sure. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. We'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... indicated that we could not take into consideration the answer. We'll consider that at a later stage. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question is the following: According to your personal experience and at any point in time in the relevant period, that is, during the war, were you able to have any view at all from this red circle to point 13. Will you tell us, please, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Throughout the war, that is from the period 1992 until the end of 1994, that is, throughout the war, this whole street was protected with screens, first of all, then a building, a part of the intersection was protected by a -- one of the buildings of the student hostels and by a coffee bar, not the bakery - a coffee bar - and along the length of the Aleja Branka Bujica Street, that is, on both the Muslim and the Serb side, there were several rows of screens from wooden boards, containers that we used to obstruct the view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, as regards these protective barricades, would you tell us whether the Aleja that you have referred to is on the map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the map is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can, bearing in mind what you've just shown us, could you try and place -- indicate the place where the barricades were on the Aleja, the barricades that you just referred to, with a black pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have just indicated three barricades or positions of barricades. Would you put the letter "B" next to each of them, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in view of the position of those barricades, did you have the possibility of having a view during the war at any time, a direct view of the point under the arrow number 13? And if no, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Because they were protected by these barricades along the length of the Aleja and the Aleja went downhill. It wasn't level. From the position number 13 there was a downward slope towards the Centre of the Blind. So it was at a lower level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Regarding the quality of obstruction of these barricades, are you emphatic in saying that a view was not possible; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I didn't have a view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. It becomes quite clear that we will not finish with this witness today, so we have to discuss how to proceed. Would you please -- if you would move to your next subject and stop so that we can discuss how we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm just going to finish with this question, and I hope we will be able to solve the problem of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My last question on this point: If you didn't have a view - and listen to my question carefully - if you did not have a direct view of what was beyond the protection barriers, can you imagine and achieve a shot, you yourself, or soldiers in general in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the presence of the witness, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can discuss it in the presence of the witness. How much time would the Defence still need for examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This rhythm and if there are no other objections -- I only have two more maps to show to the witness, and that will round up my questions about destruction. So it will be very quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it, Mr. Ierace, that you'll certainly need more than a couple of minutes for cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's true, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then we are facing a problem. Mr. DP8, we were informed that you are scheduled to travel back tomorrow. Would you be available to wait for another -- to continue -- to testify tomorrow morning and only travel back then either later tomorrow or the day after tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot continue my testimony because my sister got killed a year ago and I delayed the observation of that anniversary last Saturday and I've invited people to come and I have to be there. It is the anniversary of her death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We fully do understand that you are talking about a tragic event. When exactly would you have to be back? When do you have to be there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to be there Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Today is Thursday. Would there be a possibility -- if you would travel back later tomorrow - let's say on from 11.00 or 12.00 - and if you would arrive -- I'm not saying that this is possible, but I'm just trying to find out what your possibilities would be. Would you then arrive in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to be in Belgrade tomorrow to be able to reach home the day after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you arrive in Belgrade tomorrow later on in the day, would that be still sufficient?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be willing to continue to testify tomorrow morning if an arrangement would have been made that you could travel to Belgrade later tomorrow? I'm not saying that this is possible but just trying to find out what could be done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would mean -- the important thing is for me to get to Belgrade. I can find a bus or something. I have to reach Belgrade by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. The problem is that the alternative would be that you would return and then have to come back perhaps at a later stage to be cross-examined by the Prosecution. Of course that would be not very convenient for you; neither would it be very attractive for the Tribunal because then we have travel expenses, et cetera. So it would be good for everyone if such an arrangement could be made. But I don't know whether it's possible. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have been informed by the General there's only one connection by plane and that is the problem. Instead of going through I don't know which town, there's only one connection with Belgrade in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... about -- as you know sometimes taking a different route solves a problem of this kind. And I will -- let me say the following: If we are not able to conclude your testimony today. I'll ask the Registry to be in contact with the Victims and Witnesses Unit and see whether a solution can be found such that you would travel later tomorrow. If it was not on a direct flight, perhaps by either Frankfurt or whatever to see that you go back to Belgrade later tomorrow. If not, then of course the original schedule will be followed. But Madam Registrar has tried to get some information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the information that comes to me now indicates that there would be no other possibility. But nevertheless, we'll check whether this is the final solution. If there would be another possibility - and we also have to take into consideration visa, et cetera - if there would be a possibility to fly back tomorrow later in the day, we will invite you to reappear tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. If not, then the original schedule will be followed.
