Perhaps the ELMO could back off a little. Stop there. And could the map be pulled downwards so that we can see higher up the map -- no, the other direction. Thank you. Just there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, will you please point to the buildings which constituted the institute for blind children, or as it's sometimes called, the school for the blind or the school for blind children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, how many -- do you see on the map there are some red -- that is, dark red shapes near the intersection of Lukavicka Cesta? And Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street. Yes. I think on this map we can see two shapes which seem to indicate buildings. How many buildings were there in that complex for the Institute of the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Three buildings make the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Can you assist me with the name of the street which runs alongside them. Aleja Bosne -- what is the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: It is called Aleja Bosne Srebrene now. And that is what this map says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And does one of the buildings of the institute immediately abut that road at the intersection with Lukavicka Cesta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No. It is not right next to the intersection. It is further away from the main road there, that is, some 15 or 20 metres away from Aleja Bosne Srebrene. And that is how it should be and that is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you see that there is another red symbol immediately above and slightly to the left of the one alongside the road? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: There are two red building symbols, so it would seem, on this map; one alongside the other near that junction. Are they where you would expect to see the Institute for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I said that one of those buildings was away from the street. It was on the street. It was some 15 or 20 metres off the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Please take the ruler and lay it on the map so that one of the edges of the ruler is on one of those two buildings and the other edge points towards Ante Babica Street, that is, the intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now move the ruler slightly sideways to the right so that the edge shows us a line between the institute for blind children, as it appears on the map, and the intersection of Ante Babica and the street that runs alongside the institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it might save time if I could approach the map and place the ruler as I want it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I think you can accept from me - I'm sure the Defence will indicate if what I'm about to say is incorrect - that the intersection which the ruler crosses on Ante Babica Street is the point indicated by the dot 21 on the map you were shown earlier, and the other -- and the building --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must make an objection, since one is playing with the ruler. We've never done that. We've never played with it. Yes, indeed the ruler -- on the other hand, how do you want the witness to recognise it if the names are not exact? He's asking to speak from memory, points 21, 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness does not know, we could ask him and show him the other map. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there is such -- not a great difference by guiding the witness exactly to put the rule there where the Defence want to have it or to do it by yourself. I mean, the result in both cases is the ruler is on the place where the party that questions the witness wants the ruler to be. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. But I can imagine that the recollection of the witness as to points of certain numbers might not be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't expect him to have that recollection, and that's why I want it to be made clear to the witness by a lack of objection from the Defence that the rule is fairly placed to indicate a point of 21 on the earlier map, in terms of intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, when you cast your eye along the edge of the ruler from the school for the blind to that intersection, do you agree that it does not intersect the student hostel as it is depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a formal objection here. The witness says no [As interpreted]. One should first verify on other maps because every time we have different maps. That is what I have been always saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the witness says no or not, we -- I did not hear him say anything. Nothing was translated. And you know what the guidance is, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. What the witness says should be asked to him and not be expressed to anyone else unless it comes to us through the interpretation. That's one issue. The second issue is that I, and I think the Chamber, observed that both parties are trying to get the best out of the maps they're using.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Problems of interpretation. I did not say -- at least I think I did not say that the witness said no. The interpreter's comment it was the witness who said no during -- while Mr. Piletta-Zanin was objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because it appeared in the translation as something you said and I now understand that it was the witness who said this. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you agree that the student hostel is -- first of all, was constituted by two high-rise buildings? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And on this map they have a circle placed around them with the number "6" above the circle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I can't see the number -- oh, yes. Yes. Yes, right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. And do you agree that the way I placed the ruler was so that the edge passed over the building as indicated furthest from the street, the building of the institute for blind children? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: But this ruler could not be positioned like this, over the intersection, because you cannot see the intersection from the home for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'll come to that. But please listen to the question carefully. When you were invited by the Defence to place a ruler, and in fact I think to draw a line, from the school for the blind to that particular intersection, it passed over -- the line passed over the southern-most of the student hostel buildings. Do you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. On this map that doesn't happen, does it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So what we learn from this is that one or both of the maps are inaccurate as to the positions of at least these buildings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is speaking over the counsel. This, counsel, this is a question which is a trap, because we draw a line between two points and something is not in the middle of the thing. It is obvious that the maps do -- are not identical. So asking this question does not lead us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was Mr. Piletta-Zanin who chose to use this technique. I'm entitled to respond to it and I've made my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course you're entitled to respond to that. But if on one map the ruler crosses what appears to be a building in the map and if on the other not, I think it would be clear to the Chamber that the maps -- either one of them or both of them are different and therefore could not be correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- unless a proper explanation is given. I would say that it speaks almost for itself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown now P3279NN, photographs ending in 0, 9, and 11. Perhaps we could start off with photograph 11. I think we'll need to pan back and adjust the light on the ELMO. No, that's the wrong photograph. Could we just see the number on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, I must have given the wrong number. Your Honour -- no, that is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what appears in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. And I suggest to you that the photograph shows the view from one part of the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This is the corner of the building for the blind, and it faces Nedzarici. So this photograph seems to have been taken from a crane or something, not from the Institute for Blind Children. Next to it, right next to the wall, to the side wall facing Nedzarici. On another photograph one can see where it -- where the shopping centre was taken, the true picture -- the mirror of this wall of the Institute for the Blind, what one can see from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. So in a word, you don't accept this photograph as taken from the -- one of the buildings of the institute for blind children. Is that correct; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Next to the building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But not from the building or buildings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see the drainpipe in the top left-hand corner of the photograph, part of the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can I suggest to you that this was taken from a window on the top floor of the building closest to the street, to the intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: And I put it to you that it wasn't, because that is where I attended school, and I know the place very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You attended school at the institute for blind children? Did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Next to the Institute for the Blind was Alekse Santica primary school. Later on it became a workshop for the blind. But I attended there primary school and our school dentist had his surgery in the home for the blind. That is where we went to have our teeth repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Given your evidence earlier, in relation to the intersection of Ante Babica Street and Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street, do you say that the intersection could not be seen at all, or do you say the intersection could be seen -- in particular there were barricades which prevented one seeing the intersection itself? If it wasn't for the barricades, one could see the intersection? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: From the building of the Institute for the Blind it was not possible to see the intersection from the lines held by the Army of Republika Srpska. There were a couple of buildings -- you can see the roof here of this new building. There were three or four catering establishments with two floors, just like the Institute for the Blind and which existed, only they had been destroyed just as the building for the blind, and the Muslim soldiers used those as trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question is simply this: From the institute of blind children -- let's say in -- at the end of 1993. If it wasn't for barricades, would you have been able to see that intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At the end of 1993? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You couldn't have seen it. You couldn't have seen it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you see the barricades across the intersection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to be precise regarding the point of view. The point of this witness were three barricades, and now we're talking about barricades at the intersection. I think we should specify exactly the point of view that Mr. Ierace is referring to when putting this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a question first to the witness: Mr. DP8, you told us that this photograph seems to have been taken from a crane or something not from the institute of the blind children, next to it, right next to the wall, to the side wall facing Nedzarici. Looking at this picture, looking at the drainpipe, how far would the camera be away from that side wall, the camera that was used when taking this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm not a photographer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But you said that it was next -- right next to the wall and even -- I'm not a photographer either. Could you look at the picture and see whether that would be 30 centimetres, 1 metre, 10 metres. Try to look at the picture quite carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the distance between the home for the blind and the main road of Bosna Srebrene is 20 metre, so it could be 20 metres from the home for the blind. And here you can perfectly well see that the building itself is not right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this building then -- the building of which you see the drainpipe, is that the building of the institute for the blind children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, you told us that nevertheless you did see some barricades in the vicinity of the intersection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you that as of early October 1993 the nature of those barricades was concrete. There was a concrete barricades across part of the intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I claim that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Translation, please. I have to say I don't think I heard -- I may have to apologise. I don't think I heard in the Serbian translation "a part of." And this shade of meaning is important for Mr. Ierace. I don't think I heard it in the Serbian language. So if we want a correct answer from the witness, we need to have the question correctly translated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question, Mr. President. I'll repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You marked the positions of three barricades on a map for us earlier. The one closest to the intersection was not actually on the intersection but, rather, crossed the road closer to the Institute for the Blind, that, some distance short of the intersection itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: That first barricade next to the Institute for the Blind was behind. On this picture it was behind the shopping centre where they had their trenches and they passed along them --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Let me stop you. I'm talking of the barricade -- of the three barricades, the one that was closest to the intersection at Ante Babica Street. And what I'm putting to you is that whatever barricade was at that intersection, on the 4th of October, 1993 was concrete and was not 3 metres high or 2 metres high. It was no higher than, say, 2 metres -- in fact, it was less. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to underline that the testimony of the witness was that these barricades were 3 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that is exactly why I put to him that they were not 3 metres high.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You should not have intervened at this moment, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The barricade that on the 4th of October, 1993 existed at or near that intersection was concrete in nature and certainly not more than 2 metres high. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I do not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, might the witness be shown the second photograph. And perhaps at first he could see both photographs side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, if you compare the two photographs, I think it will become clear to you that the second shows a close-up taken from the same position as the first photograph if you look carefully at the intersection of Ante Babica Street and the street that runs alongside the institute, I think that will become clear to you. Now, my first question is this: Do you agree that the view afforded from the top floor of the institute building either from where this photograph was taken or alongside where this photograph was taken gives a view of the intersection such that barriers in the first two positions that you indicated on the map would not have blocked the view of the intersection? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No. Because this picture seems to have been taken from the roof and not from one of the floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Serb positions were at the foot of the building for blind children, on the ground floor. And that is why I claim that not a single intersection could be seen. Only along the road of Bosna Srebrene could one see the barricades positioned there from the road itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We won't take that any further at this stage. Perhaps those photographs could be removed. You told us that you went to the school for the blind as part of your duties. How many times did you go there between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Two or three times I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When were those times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Well, in the period between 1992 and 1994, so I would go there in 1992 to look around, to see how I could approach it with an armoured carrier, to pull out a wounded or killed combatant, and then again in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Are you saying that you went there only two or three times between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And are you saying the first time that you went there was essentially to scout a safe approach for any future visit you might make to the site? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: After that first visit, you only returned once, perhaps twice, before August 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the nature of your return visit? Was it to deliver food or to retrieve a body or to retrieve a wounded soldier or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: On one occasion it was to retrieve a wounded person from the line there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you arrived, was the wounded soldier inside one of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The wounded soldier was behind the building for the blind and was waiting for the APC to arrive so that he could be pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you go into the building on that occasion, since the wounded soldier was behind the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: On that occasion, no. But on the first occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. When to the best of your recollection did you go there the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: The first time was when I was touring the line, as I said, to see from where the Muslim forces may open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... when? In which month in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: In mid-1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Before September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. And the time that you retrieved the wounded person was when, the wounded soldier? What month, what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Let's say in February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you recall a third occasion or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: After that I went to the Institute for the Blind because I knew the guys who were there on the front line --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, please listen to the question. Before August of 1994, did you go there a third time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wish to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the second time that an almost aggressive tone is being used. And when the witness gives his own answers for the reasons why he went there, if he's interrupted it's not quite fair. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just reread. The witness gave his answer, but it was not a precise answer to the question. Mr. Ierace, I think I once said to Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but it's quite some time ago, that questions put nicely to a witness sometimes give the answers you are seeking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You've told us about the first time. You've told us about the second time. If you went there a third time before August 1994, when was it? In other words, what month, what year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I cannot remember with precision. I cannot remember the date or month. But in any case, it was in 1994, because as I said, we would visit all the lines in Nedzarici, those of us who were in charge of retrieving the wounded and the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you're saying it was in 1994, but you don't know whether it was before, during, or after August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And on that occasion, whenever it was in 1994, did you go inside any of the buildings at the institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I said that I entered on the first occasion and that I looked around to see what could be seen from the positions held by soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the first occasion. That was in mid-1992. When you went there in 1994, did you go into any of the buildings of the institute for blind children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How long were you there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I spent an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. And I think you started to say that you knew some of the people that were there, some of the soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it a social visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. What was the purpose -- what was the work purpose for you to be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: In order to see again how I can access the area and for them to show me roughly from which positions they could target me with mortars, Zoljas, Osas from where I could be hit when I come with a transporter to fetch the wounded. So that was our practice throughout the war, to tour the lines, to see from what positions we might be targeted and therefore to protect myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, until now I tried to make an inventory. There's one, at least one question from the Bench. So would you please -- and we also are informed that transportation to the Detention Unit could not take place after 7.00, so would you please keep that in mind for the next 14 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you went inside -- I withdraw that. You told us that a platoon had responsibility for that building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. And did you notice inside the manner in which the platoon protected themselves from fire from the other side? For instance, were there sandbags inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Because the building had a number of large windows that faced onto the enemy, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: From that side -- on that side there were no windows. There were just a concrete wall, and on the right-hand side facing the Federation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think this is a trap, in view of what we know and what we heard as testimony. The witness has answered, but I wanted to say that this method of proceeding seems to me to be a trap, a question to trap the witness in view of what we know from the proceedings so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We know a lot about a lot of buildings. I think it's not a question that would not be admissible in cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also object to the expression of that intervention in the presence of the witness with his headphones on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, I suggest to you that there were windows in those buildings which could be seen from the ABiH side. In particular, across the shopping centre, the high-rise buildings on the other side had a view of the windows in the institute, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: From the shopping centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. And that, I take it, was obviously the reason that there were sandbags inside the institute, to protect the soldiers from fire coming in through the windows. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: On that side there were no sandbags, because the line was not on that side because that building which you say has windows was facing the old school, the elementary school I went to, and that building was a Serb position. So from the old school, the position was again facing the shopping centre, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Did you go upstairs on that visit in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: One of the buildings had a ground plus two floors, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you go into that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I entered all the buildings that were part of the Institute for the Blind. So I entered that one as well, though I don't know which one you mean. The first one next to the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Were there two buildings that had ground plus two floors, as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you go upstairs in either of the two buildings in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No. Because that would be equal to suicide. It was all exposed and ruined and could be seen from all the buildings, especially from the Oslobodjne building and the new old people's home, from the student hostels, from Vojnicko Polje. It was -- one would be seen as on the palm of one's hand. So as far as I know, no one went up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you don't know whether there were sandbags upstairs or not because you didn't go up. Is that the position? I'm talking now about the first floor and second floor of those two buildings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I told you that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but the witness has just said that he didn't go upstairs, so why is he being asked whether he knows or doesn't know whether there were sandbags when he said that he didn't go upstairs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An objection to a question is not asking why a question is put but if it's a question that's not admissible. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is that correct? Because you did not go upstairs in those two buildings, you don't know what measures there might have been upstairs to protect soldiers from fire from ABiH positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I'm telling you that the trenches of the Serbian army were on the bottom floors, and it was not possible to make a trench on any one of the floors of the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. I'm not asking about the trenches, but we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown P3274, photographs 95 and 96. And perhaps I could see them quickly before they go to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. Ierace, it's P3274B and P3274C.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Yes, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace asked to have a look at them quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you show the witness B first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have only one question in the re-examination. I just wish to tell you that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you conclude in approximately three minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the view which appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you agree that it's a photograph looking towards the direction of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This is -- these are houses belonging to the airport settlement, and the Muslims held these houses --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. Please listen to the question. As you look up the street in the middle of the photograph, do you agree that it's in the direction of Nedzarici? In other words, if you -- as the crow flies, if you continued in that direction, eventually you would come to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the map for sniping incident 22.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: At the end of Nedzarici. To the end of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's the Defence exhibit which was shown to the witness earlier. I think it is 1773. Might that be placed on the ELMO quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see number -- the dot with an arrow alongside and a number 22 on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the ELMO please pan back. Thank you. Further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see the dot indicated by the number 22. Please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you accept that the photograph shows the view from the area of the dot number 22 looking up that long road towards Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. The whole of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you agree that the photograph was taken from around point 22 looking west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: This photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't. All right. Would you please look at the map and with the pointer first place the pointer on the dot indicated by number 22.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, move the pointer along the road to the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: Here you can see just these two first buildings in Dobrinja, which lean on the Muslim settlement. But there are some other buildings on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Please wait. All right. All right. All right. I take it therefore from what you just said that you understand that the photograph shows us the view if you stand around point 22 and look up that street that you just indicated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's as far as I can go in the time. I do require further time. I will review how much I have left to go, and at some stage indicate that to the Trial Chamber and also the topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, one question you said you have. Not two or three, which means a couple or more, but one question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None, but an observation. The bank has exploded even in the system of banking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's do that tomorrow when the witness has left, and not discuss this at this very moment when the Bench also has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us, Witness DP8, that in front of the institute for theology, there were pine trees. You also told us that they had not been felled during the war. You didn't say anything about after the war. Were they then felled, or do you know, or do you know that they were not felled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I don't know about the period after the war. I didn't go there. I know that the convent itself was renovated because after the signing of the Dayton Agreement, I left my home and left that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP8
utterances.text: I moved out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP8, this concludes your testimony in this court. The Chamber is aware that the Prosecution might not agree that this concludes the testimony in this court, but that's a procedural issue that -- that we have to discuss later, whether to see whether this witness for this reason should be recalled. So I'm not guaranteeing you that you do not have to return; but as it stands now, this would conclude your examination. As you may have noticed, everyone did their utmost best in order to make it possible for you to leave The Hague tomorrow and to return. So whether it's a final thank to you that you came and asked -- answered the questions of both parties and the Bench or that is just provisionally thanking you is not for the full 100 per cent certain. But one thing is certain: That I wish you at least tomorrow a safe trip to your home country. Madam Usher, you may escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the record indicate that the witness waved towards the accused as he left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The witness greeted me in a cordial manner, and I greeted him in return.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think that as a general rule, we should refrain from everything that is not functional for these proceedings, whether it's waving, whether it's whatever other gesture. Professionals should do that, and everyone should do that in this courtroom. I think that should be clear. I didn't see it, so I can't comment on it. I could have a look at the video pictures, but I don't know whether it's necessary to do that. It may be clear for everyone that all non-functional gestures should be avoided to the extent possible, but I'm aware that you can't stop your eyes moving. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00. If there's any issue as far as the recalling of this witness is concerned, the Chamber would like to hear from that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean 9.00 tomorrow morning, Mr. President, or later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not specifically tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, the witness leaves anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 7.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
